items.stem: Why does simply using a very large context window not fully solve long-document tasks?

options.text: Attention cost grows with context and models may weight middle content poorly
options.rationale: Correct: long context raises cost and can suffer the lost-in-the-middle effect.

options.text: Large windows make the model smaller
options.rationale: Window size does not shrink the model.

options.text: Long context removes the need for a prompt
options.rationale: A prompt is still required regardless of window size.

options.text: Large windows guarantee perfect recall of every token

items.explanation: Correct: long context raises cost and can suffer the lost-in-the-middle effect.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO strategies help an assistant answer over documents larger than a comfortable prompt? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Chunk the documents and retrieve only the relevant pieces
options.rationale: Correct: retrieval keeps the prompt focused and affordable.
Correct: hierarchical summarisation compresses long input while keeping key facts.

options.text: Paste the entire corpus into every request regardless of cost
options.rationale: That is expensive and can trigger lost-in-the-middle issues.
The question is needed to retrieve and answer.

items.explanation: Correct: retrieval keeps the prompt focused and affordable.

items.stem: Key information sits in the middle of a long prompt and the model ignores it. What mitigation is most appropriate?

options.text: Reorder or rerank so the most relevant context is prominently placed
options.rationale: Correct: placing key content where the model attends well counters lost-in-the-middle.
Temperature does not fix positional attention weaknesses.
Removing context loses the needed information.
Modality change is irrelevant to text positioning.

items.explanation: Correct: placing key content where the model attends well counters lost-in-the-middle.
